question: How much do RAPM, ORAPM, DRAPM and the six factors move when the games in the fit window are resampled?
inputs: 1Y regular-season impact-ratings-v1-method fits for 2014-15 to 2025-26 (sealed artifacts for 2023-24 to 2025-26, courtlens-impact-history-v1 artifacts before)
method: Game bootstrap: draw the window's games with replacement (as many draws as games); a game drawn k times multiplies its observations' weights by k, so all stints and both sides of a game stay together.
Each replicate refits the same design with the fit's already selected alpha (no reselection) and the fit's own centering (seconds weighted by the replicate's multiplicities; decayed for time decay).
Targets: RAPM (offense, defense, total) and the six factors (oTS, oTOV, oREB, dTS, dTOV, dREB) for 1Y fits; RAPM for time-decay fits.
Random stream: numpy default_rng(SeedSequence([2501, starting_year, fit_code])), fit_code 1 = 1Y, 2 = time decay; replicate r uses the r-th draw.
Served values: 10th and 90th percentiles and replicate standard deviation, for every player with a point estimate; display qualification is unchanged.
uncertainty: This is the interval itself. It is a game-resampling interval around a shrunk estimate with a fixed penalty, not a confidence interval for true impact.
evaluation: Check: the bootstrap code's replicate with all multiplicities equal to 1 reproduces the point-estimate coefficients (max absolute difference below 1e-8)
Per season: median 80% interval width for qualified players, by metric, and the share of qualified players whose interval excludes zero
acceptance: 200 replicates for every 1Y fit 2014-15 to 2025-26 and every time-decay season-end fit
Two runs reproduce identical interval artifact hashes
outputs: data/derived/impact-intervals-v1/ interval artifacts keyed by the fitted artifact hash
limitations: A fixed alpha and lineup confounding make intervals narrower than the true uncertainty
No claim that one player is better than another is made from overlapping intervals
negative_result_policy: Publish interval widths whatever they are, including if most intervals include zero.
